papers.titleEn: Local Symmetry Breaking Facilitates Near-Infrared Circularly Polarized Lanthanide Emission in Perovskite Nanocrystals
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Imparting chiroptical activity of lanthanide transitions provides an attractive route to circularly polarized luminescence. However, obtaining intense emission from their Laporte-forbidden f–f transitions while also generating significant rotatory strength remains a formidable challenge in materials design. This work establishes a platform for efficient near-infrared (NIR) circularly polarized luminescence (CPL), centered on the telecom-relevant C-band around 1550 nm, from lanthanide dopants (Yb3+/Er3+) embedded in chiral perovskite nanocrystal (CsPbX3) hosts. Atomic-scale structural analyses reveal a preferential enrichment of lanthanide concentration near the nanocrystal surfaces, where chiral ligands distort the lattice, lowering the local symmetry. Spectroscopic measurements confirm the highly efficient host-to-dopant energy transfer, facilitating strong CPL, with a luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) of 0.36 and a CPL brightness (BCPL) of 4.2 × 105 M–1 cm–1 at 1550 nm, representing nearly four orders of magnitude above the previous benchmark. With improved photostability, these results establish lanthanide-doped chiral perovskite nanocrystals as a promising route to telecom-relevant CPL.
papers.filename: Mengxia Liu, J. Am. Chem. Soc., 2026, Local Symmetry Breaking Facilitates Near-Infrared Circularly Polarized Lanthanide Emission in Perovskite Nanocrystals

papers.titleEn: Solution-State Supramolecular Engineering of Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbazole‐based self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs), exemplified by [4‐(3,6‐dimethyl‐9H‐carbazol‐9‐yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (Me‐4PACz), are widely used as hole‐selective contacts in efficient perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs). However, aggregation‐driven intermolecular organization in solution adversely affects the homogenization of SAMs on the substrate, compromising the performance of tandem devices. Herein, a supramolecular co‐assembly strategy is developed to modulate solution‐state intermolecular organization and suppress aggregation by introducing 4‐fluorophenylglycine hydrochloride, which co‐assembles with Me‐4PACz via dual‐site non‐covalent interactions. This strategy links solution‐state modulation to the formation of uniform SAM films, simultaneously realizing optimized energy alignment and reducing residual stress at the buried interface. Champion power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 23.66% and 33.91% (certified 33.5%) are achieved for 1.67 eV wide‐bandgap perovskite solar cells and 1 cm 2 two‐terminal monolithic perovskite/silicon TSCs, respectively. Moreover, the optimized tandem devices exhibit excellent operational stability under the ISOS‐L‐2 protocol, retaining 91% of the initial PCE after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking under one‐sun continuous illumination.
papers.filename: Wenzhong Shen, Adv. Funct. Mater., 2026, Solution-State Supramolecular Engineering of Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Perovskite Silicon Tandem Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: Unlocking Near-Unity Photoluminescence Quantum Yield for Cs 3 TbCl 6 Perovskite Nanocrystals Via Fluoroquinolone Surface Engineering
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Rare‐earth‐based lead‐free halide perovskite nanocrystals (NCs) are promising for optoelectronics due to their narrow‐band emission and physicochemical stability. However, the intrinsic 4f‐4f forbidden transitions of rare‐earth ions result in limited absorption cross‐sections. Furthermore, inevitable surface defects at the nanoscale trigger non‐radiative recombination, limiting luminescence efficiency. Herein, a surface engineering strategy utilizing fluoroquinolone (FQ) molecules is proposed to construct a hybrid system. Specifically, by introducing norfloxacin (NFLX) as a surface ligand, NFLX‐modified Cs 3 TbCl 6 nanocrystals (NCs) have been developed that achieve a near‐unity photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 99.67%. Experiments and theoretical analyses reveal that the organic ligands effectively passivate surface defects, thereby suppressing non‐radiative transitions. Simultaneously, the ligand acts as an efficient antenna that amplifies excitation light capture and establishes energy transfer pathways to NCs. Notably, it is demonstrated that beyond energy level matching, the electronic effects, steric configurations, and absorption capacities of ligand are crucial factors for efficient antenna effect. Finally, the effectiveness of this strategy is validated through applications in extreme‐environment‐resilient fluorescent anti‐counterfeiting fibers and high‐quality white light‐emitting diodes (WLEDs). This work overcomes the bottleneck limiting the luminescence efficiency of rare‐earth halide NCs, paving a new technical pathway for the design of high‐efficiency surface‐coordinated hybrid rare‐earth luminescent NCs.
papers.filename: Baojiu Chen, Adv. Funct. Mater., 2026, Unlocking Near-Unity Photoluminescence Quantum Yield for Cs 3 TbCl 6 Perovskite Nanocrystals Via Fluoroquinolone Surface Engineering

papers.titleEn: MBWCT-Net: Multiscale Transient Learning for Early Discrimination of Wood-Extracted VOC Mixtures via an Electronic Nose
papers.abstract: Abstract Metal oxide semiconductor electronic noses offer a compact and nondestructive method for volatile organic compound (VOC) analysis. However, reliable recognition of multicomponent mixtures remains challenging because of sensor cross-sensitivity, nonlinear adsorption–desorption dynamics, sensor drift, and long acquisition cycles. Eucalyptus, Rosewood, and Sandalwood essential oils were used as controlled plant-derived VOC benchmarks. Static-headspace gas chromatography–mass spectrometry showed partially shared constituents but distinct dominant headspace fingerprints: Eucalyptus was rich in eucalyptol and monoterpenes, Rosewood was linalool-dominant, and Sandalwood showed a substantially different and partly unresolved profile. The three samples therefore did not exhibit uniformly high compositional similarity. We developed MBWCT-Net, a physics-motivated Multi-Branch Wavelet CNN–Transformer Network that combines a Multi-Scale Wavelet Parallel Network, Lightweight Cross-Attention, and a Multi-Scale Adaptive Transformer to model multiscale response components, cross-band coupling, and local–global temporal dependencies. Under an identical five-fold protocol, MBWCT-Net achieved 95.37 ± 0.61% accuracy and 95.37 ± 0.66% weighted F1, outperforming both raw-input and wavelet-enhanced baselines. Using the first 45 s of the transient response, accuracy reached 94.61 ± 0.70%, within 0.76 percentage points of the complete 60 s response. Deployment on an RK3588 platform yielded a single-sample inference latency of 12.4 ± 0.8 ms and a memory footprint of 48.5 MB. These measurements characterize computational feasibility and do not represent the duration of the complete sensing cycle. Response plots from three independent measurements and normalization-shape checks assessed short-term repeatability and preprocessing effects. Quantitative high-dimensional feature metrics and measured-noise physical-validity analyses evaluated class separability and the preservation of temporal morphology, respectively.
papers.filename: Shari L. Forbes, ACS Sens., 2026, MBWCT-Net Multiscale Transient Learning for Early Discrimination of Wood-Extracted VOC Mixtures via an Electronic Nose

papers.titleEn: Polymer-agnostic crosslinking enables robust high-temperature dielectrics for energy storage
papers.abstract: Capacitive energy storage under high operating temperatures and electric fields exceeds the limits of most commercial polymers. While crosslinking can, in principle, enhance electro-thermal stability of polymers, conventional approaches remain severely constrained by their reliance on polymer-specific chemistries and often introduce defects that compromise insulation. Herein we present a polymer-agnostic crosslinking platform based on nitrene-mediated C–H insertion, enabling substantial performance and stability improvement across chemically diverse commercial dielectric polymers. Using polyetherimide as a benchmark, the crosslinked film delivers a discharged energy density of 6.0 J cm−3 with >90% efficiency at 200 °C, along with robust cycling stability ( > 1 × 105 cycles) under harsh operational conditions (at 500 MV m−1) and a projected service lifetime of 60 years under standard industrial fields. This work establishes a facile and practical pathway to upgrade existing industrial polymers for reliable operation under harsh environments. In capacitive energy storage systems, crosslinking can improve polymer electrothermal stability, but conventional approaches rely on polymer-specific chemistries and often introduce defects that compromise insulating performance. Here the authors present a polymer-agnostic crosslinking platform based on nitrene mediated C–H insertion that improves performance and stability across a wide range of commercial dielectric polymers.
papers.filename: Yi Liu, Nat. Commun., 2026, Polymer-agnostic crosslinking enables robust high-temperature dielectrics for energy storage

papers.titleEn: Composition-Dependent Interfacial Energetics in p - i - n Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Compositional engineering offers a direct route to tuning the absorber band structure and interfacial energy alignment in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). We systematically varied the formamidinium (FA)/methylammonium (MA) and I/Br ratios in Cs0.05(FAxMA1–x)0.95Pb(IxBr1–x)3 perovskites to examine how composition governs charge extraction, interfacial recombination, and photovoltaic performance in p–i–n-structured devices. Increasing the FA and I content gradually narrowed the optical bandgap through the progressive shift in the perovskite band edges, which in turn modified the band offset at the interfaces with both p- and n-type selective contacts. The resultant photovoltaic performance of p–i–n devices (MeO-2PACz/perovskite/C60) was monitored closely with composition across the series, reaching an optimum at x = 0.93. Impedance spectroscopy confirmed that carrier extraction efficiency and recombination dynamics are governed by the composition-dependent interfacial band alignment and defect density.
papers.filename: Hui‐Seon Kim, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2026, Composition-Dependent Interfacial Energetics in p - i - n Perovskite Solar Cells
